Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:10:1.hebrew: אך בכור שור כו' - מדמצי למיכתב "אך שור כשב ועז", דהא עניינא בבכור קמישתעי, דכתיב לעיל מיניה: "כל פטר רחם" וגו', ונקט בכולהו "בכור" — ש"מ: עד שיהא הבכור כאמו, ולא יהא דומה לאחר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:10:1.english: “But the firstborn of an ox,” etc. - Since [the verse] could have written “However, an ox, a sheep, and a goat,” for the subject matter is [already] speaking of a firstborn, as it is written before it: “Everything that opens the womb...” (Numbers 18:15), yet it specified “firstborn” for each of them — learn from this: [firstborn status applies only] when the firstborn is like its mother, and it does not resemble another [species].

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:11:1.english: “But” makes a distinction - For all instances of akh and rak in the Torah [serve] to exclude.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:12:1.english: But doesn’t the tanna - [The tanna] of our Mishnah.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:12:2.hebrew: פטר פטר קנסיב לה לפרה - דקא מפיק פרה שילדה מין חמור דפטורה מן הבכורה מן פטר פטר, עד שיהא היולד חמור והולד חמור, ופרה נמי גמרה מחמור. ורב יהודה, היכי שבק קרא דמתניתין וקנסיב למודא אחרינא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:12:2.english: Cites “firstborn,” “firstborn,” with regard to a cow - For [the Tanna] derives that a cow that gave birth to a donkey-like [offspring] is exempt from the [law of the] firstborn from “firstborn,” “firstborn” — [teaching] that the one giving birth must be a donkey and the offspring [must be] a donkey, and a cow likewise learns from a donkey. And Rav Yehuda, how could he abandon the verse of our Mishnah and adopt a different derivation?

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:13:1.hebrew: רב יהודה - דאמר כרבי יוסי הגלילי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:13:1.english: Rav Yehuda - [He is the one] who says [this] in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:15:1.hebrew: גלי רחמנא - בחמור, דקדושת דמים הוא — שאינו קדוש [אלא] (בלא) דמיו, שיפדהו בשה — גלי ביה רחמנא דנדמה פטור, וה"ה לבכור בהמה טהורה, דקדושת הגוף היא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:15:1.english: The Merciful One revealed - In [the case of] a donkey, which is [subject to] sanctity of value — for it is not holy [except for] its monetary value, in that one redeems it with a lamb — the Merciful One revealed regarding it that [an offspring that] resembles [another species] is exempt; and the same applies to the firstborn of a kosher animal, which is [subject to] inherent sanctity.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:18:1.hebrew: למה נאמרו אימורי כו' - בהאי קרא: "אך בכור שור או בכור כשב או בכור עז לא תפדה, קדש הם, ואת דמם תזרוק ואת חלבם תקטיר" — דכולם אימוריהם קרבים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:18:1.english: Why were the sacrificial portions of, etc., stated - In this verse: "Howbeit the firstborn of an ox, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy; and their blood you shall dash, and their fat you shall burn" — for the sacrificial portions of all of them are offered.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:19:1.hebrew: שור - נסכיו מרובים: חצי ההין, וכשב ועז — רביעית ההין. כשב — אלייתו קריבה עם אימורים, כדמפרש בויקרא, מה שאין כן בשור ועז:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:19:1.english: An ox - Its libations are greater: half a hin, whereas [for] a sheep and a goat [they are] a quarter of a hin. [Regarding] a sheep — its fat tail is offered with the sacrificial portions, as is explained in Leviticus, which is not the case with an ox or a goat.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:1:1.hebrew: והא מאתן וארבעים דינר נינהו - אלא כפול היה, ובמנה דקודש הוו מאתן. והנך ארבעים דטפו עלייהו — זהו שהוסיפו בימי יחזקאל, והוסיפו עליהן שתות, דארבעין הוו שתותא מלבר; דבמאתן איכא ה' פעמים מ', והביאו פעם מ' ששית מבחוץ והוסיפו עליהן, ולא אמרי' שתות מלגיו — שיחלקו לששה ויוסיפו על המשקל אחד מאותן חלקים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:1:1.english: But these are two hundred and forty dinars - Rather, [the Sanctuary maneh] was double, and in the Sanctuary maneh there were two hundred [dinars]. And those forty that were extra upon them — that is what they added in the days of Ezekiel; and they added a sixth to them, as forty is a sixth [calculated] from the outside. For in two hundred there are five times forty, and they brought a sixth [instance of] forty from the outside and added [it] to them; and we do not say [that it is] a sixth from the inside, that they should divide [the two hundred] into six and add one of those parts to the weight.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:23:1.hebrew: כשב ועז - פסח בא מהן, דכתיב: ״מן הכבשים ומן העזים תקחו״:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:23:1.english: A sheep and a goat - The Paschal offering comes from them, as it is written: “You shall take it from the sheep or from the goats” (Exodus 12:5).

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:24:1.hebrew: שור ועז נתרבו אצל עבודת כוכבים בציבור - פר לעולה, ושעיר לחטאת:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:24:1.english: An ox and a goat were included with regard to communal idol worship - [Namely,] a bull for a burnt offering and a he-goat for a sin offering:

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:25:1.hebrew: שור וכשב יש בהן צד ריבוי אצל מזבח - דכשהן קרבים, יש מהן לאשים יותר מעז: שור בנסכים, וכשב באליה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:25:1.english: An ox and a lamb have an element of increase with regard to the altar - For when they are offered, there is more from them for the fire-offerings than from a goat: an ox in [its] libations, and a lamb in [its fat] tail.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:26:1.hebrew: א"כ - דלא אתיא קרא אלא להכי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:26:1.english: If so - That the verse comes only for this.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:29:1.hebrew: ועדיין אני אומר פטר חמור תפדה בשה - ולא בדבר אחר, ושאר בכורי טמאה בכל דבר, ולעולם קדושים בבכורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:29:1.english: And still I can say: “The firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb” - and not with anything else, while the rest of the firstborn of an impure [animal may be redeemed] with anything, and [they are] nonetheless sanctified with [the status of] a firstborn.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:3:1.english: In the house of the great session - In the great study hall.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:4:1.english: That they slackened their hands, etc. - Therefore, Amalek came upon them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:4:2.english: The fathers look not back to their children (to save them) because of feebleness of hands - From here it is derived that they slackened their hands from the Torah.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:5:1.english: In matters of folly - To commit harlotry with the daughters of Moab.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:6:1.hebrew: ערומות פגעו בהן - ותקראן משמע, גופן היה פוגע בהן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:6:1.english: Naked [women] encountered them - “Vatikrena” implies that their bodies were encountering them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:6:2.english: That they all became those who experienced seminal emissions - And it is an expression of [seminal] emission [mikreh].

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:7:1.hebrew: פטר חמור פטר חמור שני פעמים - כתובים בתורה: חד בקדש לי כל בכור (שמות י״ג:ב׳), וחד בראה אתה (שם לד):
Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:7:1.english: “Firstborn of a donkey,” “firstborn of a donkey,” twice - [They] are written in the Torah: one in [the passage of] “Sanctify to Me every firstborn” (Exodus 13:2), and one in [the passage of] “See, You” (ibid. 34).

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:7:2.english: The one giving birth - The mother.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:7:3.english: And the [animal] born is a donkey - That it resembles its mother.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:8:1.english: And what are they with regard to consumption - Those that do not resemble their mother.

Rashi on Bekhorot 5b:9:1.english: Some of the characteristics - Of its mother.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 5b:11:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר אך חלק - תימה: תנא דידן, דלית ליה הך דרשא — מקצת סימן חייב, מנא ליה? ומתני' היא פ"ב (לקמן בכורות דף טז:), ולא מיסתבר דפליג אהא דפירקין. ומיהו, אי לא פליגי, קשה: דמייתי עלה דתנא כרב יהודה; וכי קאמר מה"מ, הוה ליה לאיתויי קרא דמתני':
Tosafot on Bekhorot 5b:11:1.english: “The verse states: ‘But,’ [which] makes a distinction” - It is puzzling: As for the Tanna of our [Mishnah], who does not accept this exposition — from where does he [derive that if the offspring has] partial characteristics, it is obligated? And it is a Mishnah in the second chapter (below, Bekhorot 16b), and it is not reasonable [to say] that it disputes that [Mishnah] of our chapter. However, if they do not disagree, it is difficult: for [the Gemara] cites regarding it that the Tanna [holds] in accordance with Rav Yehuda; and when it asks: “From where are these matters [derived]?” it should have cited the verse of our Mishnah!

Tosafot on Bekhorot 5b:12:1.hebrew: והא תנא פטר פטר נסיב לה לפרה - ואין לומר: מ"מ איצטריך קרא דמתני' לפטור מקדושת פטר חמור, וקרא דהכא לפטור מדין שור — ד"פטור מן הבכורה" דקתני במתני' משמע דלגמרי פטר לה לפרה, מכלל ד"פטר פטר" דילפי' מהדדי, כדלקמן. וא"ת: נהי דשמעינן מ"פטר פטר" פרה שילדה מין סוס, דילמא ה"מ היכא דאשתני לדבר שאינו קדוש קדושת הגוף; אבל כגון רחל שילדה מין עז, דקדוש קדושת הגוף, הוה אמינא דקדשא? וי"ל: דמסתבר לגמרי (משמע) דילפינן מהדדי קדושת דמים מקדושת הגוף, כדאמר בסמוך. וקשה: דהא אמר: אפילו קדושת הגוף מקדושת הגוף לא ילפי', דהא לשור וכשב ועז צריך קרא לכל חד וחד:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 5b:12:1.english: "But doesn't the tanna cite 'firstborn, firstborn' with regard to a cow" - And one cannot say: In any case, the verse of the Mishnah was needed to exempt [the offspring] from the sanctity of the firstborn of a donkey, and the verse here [in the Gemara] to exempt [it] from the law of an ox — for "exempt from the firstborn," which is taught in the Mishnah, implies that it completely exempts the cow, from the fact that [through] "firstborn, firstborn" we derive [them] from one another, as [the Gemara explains] below. And if you say: Granted that we learn from "firstborn, firstborn" [regarding] a cow that gave birth to a horse of sorts; perhaps this applies only where it changed into something that is not holy with bodily sanctity, but in a case such as a ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts, which is holy with bodily sanctity, I would have said that it is sanctified? And one can say: It is entirely logical (meaning) that we derive them from one another — sanctity of value from bodily sanctity, as [the Gemara] says nearby. And [yet] it is difficult, for behold, [the Gemara] says that even [one] bodily sanctity from [another] bodily sanctity we do not derive, as for an ox, a lamb, and a goat a verse is needed for each and every one.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 5b:26:1.hebrew: ורבי יוסי הגלילי אם כן ליכתוב קרא אך בכור שור וכשב ועז - והא דדרשינן מינה "עד שיהא שור ובכורו שור", אע"ג דאיצטריך לכדר' יוסי בר חנינא — משום דכעין בכור שני ושלישי יש לנו לדרוש מן הראשון:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 5b:26:1.english: "And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: If so, let the verse write: 'But a firstborn ox, and a lamb, and a goat'" - And that which we derive from it: "until [the mother] is an ox and its firstborn is an ox," even though [this mention of "firstborn"] was needed for [the teaching] of Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina — [that is] because just like the second and third [mentions of] "firstborn," we are to derive [the same] from the first [as well].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 5b:3:1.hebrew: תשעים חמורים לובים - ע"ש (נחום ג׳:ט׳): "פוט ולובים היו בעזרתך", ו"לובים וכושי' במצעדיו". "חמרא לובאה", ר"פ במה בהמה (שבת דף נא:) — פירש בערוך: "חמור מצרי". ובירושלמי [גריס]: גרים הבאים מפוט ולוב, מהו להמתין ג' דורות:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 5b:3:1.english: "Ninety Libyan donkeys" - [Named] after [the verse]: (Nahum 3:9) "Put and Lubim were your help," and [the verse: (Daniel 11:43)] "and the Lubim and Cushim were at his steps." [Regarding] "a Libyan donkey" at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Bameh Behemah (Shabbat 51b), the Arukh explained: "An Egyptian donkey." And in the Yerushalmi [the text reads]: "Converts who come from Put and Luv, what is [the halakhah regarding whether they must] wait three generations?"
